newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Ward says Sears recruiting halted.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Ward says Sears recruiting halted.

text.p: Montgomery Ward Holding Co said a U.S. Bankruptcy Court granted a temporary order restraining Sears, Roebuck and Co from approaching, contacting or soliciting for employment any current management employee of Montgomery Ward.

The restraining order was granted based on a motion by Montgomery Ward which alleged predatory recruiting practices by Sears designed to "hasten the weakening state of Montgomery Ward" and "make it even more difficult for (Ward) to do business," Montgomery Ward said in a news release.

Montgomery Ward filed for bankruptcy on July 7, 1997. "Despite the fact that we are in a competitive business, we have a crystal clear policy of matters such as this," said Sears spokesman Ron Culp. "If this indeed happened, it was against these guidelines and we will take appropriate actions to see this doesn't happen again," he said, adding, "We will also reissue the policy today."

Culp said the policy deals with guidelines when a competitor is failing. In dealing with job applicants, "It lets them contact us," and cautions against not being over zealous or overly aggressive at pursuing employees at another company, he said.

Montgomery Ward alleged that the Sears "Action Plan" was distributed via E-mail to Sears field locations and targeted specific key positions for recruiting efforts solely in order to hurt Montgomery Ward's business. It told Sears personnel to be "extremely predatory" in their methods, Ward said.

Sears human resource representatives began systematically contacting Montgomery Ward personnel in targeted jobs, and recruiters were told to keep a headcount of how many people they could hire away, Montgomery Ward said.

"Obviously our first priority is to fix our business and we believe that we can compete with any retailer in a fair business environment. However, based on this 'Action Plan' we believe that Sears has crossed the line between healthy competition and unethical activities," said Roger Goddu, chairman and chief executive officer of Montgomery Ward.

Montgomery Ward is the largest privately held retailer in the United States, currently operating a chain of 400 stores in 43 states. Upon the closing of its specialty stores, Montgomery Ward will operate 356 stores in 39 states.
